newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: LG Metals plunges on losses reports.
newsitem.headline: LG Metals plunges on losses reports.

text.p: Shares in South Korea's LG Metals plunged from the market's opening bell on Wednesday on local newspaper reports, denied by the company, that the firm was facing losses from metal futures trading, brokers said.
The stock opened the day at its lower limit of 12,300 won, down 1,000 won. It later recovered to 12,400 won.

The Korea Economic Daily newspaper reported on Wednesday that LG Metals was facing losses from its speculative metal futures trading on the London Metal Exchange (LME) and the government had begun an investigation into the company.
Officials with LG Metals denied that the company was facing such losses from large short positions on the LME.
"We are not facing losses from metal futures trading and we have not been informed of any investigation by the government," an LG official, who declined to be named, told Reuters.
A Finance Ministry official also denied that the government had started an investigation into LG Metals' futures trading.
"There has been no confirmation on whether LG Metals was speculatively trading futures and faced losses from that," the ministry official said.
Three month copper prices rose to $2,200 a tonne during Tuesday afternoon LME trading, as the market geared up for Wednesday's February option declarations.
LG Metals, a unit of LG Group LUGG.CN, is South Korea's largest producer of copper, gold and silver.
